title: Feature detection and graceful degradation
learningObjectives: Explain feature detection and graceful degradation and apply secure, accessible, maintainable browser practices.

understand.concept: Feature detection checks whether an API or CSS capability exists before using it. Use capability checks such as 'IntersectionObserver' in window or CSS.supports(). Graceful degradation keeps essential content and core actions usable when an enhancement is unavailable.
understand.whyItMatters: Browser support varies by version and environment. Capability checks and fallbacks prevent a feature from becoming a single point of failure.
understand.analogy: Feature detection checks whether a tool is available while keeping a basic method ready.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser security, accessibility, and performance rules depend on platform behaviour and server configuration.

explain.narrative: The branch selects an enhancement only when the API exists. The fallback remains usable without the API.

examples.code: if('IntersectionObserver'in window){console.log('Use lazy loading observer')}else{console.log('Load images eagerly as a fallback')}
examples.explanation: The branch selects an enhancement only when the API exists. The fallback remains usable without the API.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the security or reliability principle.

practise.guidedTask: Choose a browser API and implement a feature check plus a usable fallback. Test the fallback path explicitly.
practise.independentTask: Review a small browser feature for security, accessibility, performance, and lifecycle risks. Add a fallback and document the server-side controls required.
hints: Treat all browser and network input as untrusted.
Use exact origin checks and least privilege.
Measure performance and clean up resources.
